title: Java Programming
description: Work with core Java basics such as console output, loops, and arrays. The simulation tab provides a directly editable Java code editor.
example1Text: The smallest Java program with a main method and a console print statement.
example2Text: A for loop is the standard way to repeat the same instruction several times.
example3Text: An integer array can be sorted in ascending order with Arrays.sort.
example4Text: Provide values in the input field beforehand and read them line- and token-wise using Scanner.nextLine() and Scanner.nextInt().
exercise1Desc: Write a Java program that prints Hello World to the console exactly once.
exercise2Desc: Use a loop to print Hello World to the console exactly five times.
exercise3Desc: Add two integer values and print the sum in the console.
exercise4Desc: Sort an integer array in ascending order and print the result afterwards.
exercise5Desc: Iterate over an array and determine the largest contained value.

commandOverview.title: What works in the Java editor?
commandOverview.limitationsText: Write one Main.java-style program. You can run Java source code, but you cannot type terminal commands into the editor.

basics.title: Basic Java syntax
basics.description: Basic Java syntax works: variables, operators, if/else, switch, and method calls.

loops.title: Loops and control flow
loops.description: for, while, do/while, and for-each work for exercises and small algorithms.

arraysCollections.title: Arrays, lists, maps, and sets
arraysCollections.description: Arrays and typical java.util collections work: Arrays.sort, ArrayList, LinkedList, HashMap, HashSet, Collections.sort.

objects.title: Own types
objects.description: Custom classes, constructors, enums, records, interfaces, and static methods can be placed in the same editor file.

output.title: Console output

standardLibrary.title: Standard library subset
standardLibrary.description: Common library classes from java.lang, java.util, java.math, and simple java.time are available. OS-facing APIs are not reliable.

singleFile.title: One editor file

input.title: Console input (Scanner & System.in)
input.description:
How to use console input in the browser simulator:

1. Initialization in code:
• Import the Scanner class: import java.util.Scanner;
• Create the Scanner object: Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in);

2. Input methods:
• sc.nextLine() reads the next full line up to the line break (Enter) as a String.
• sc.next() reads the next individual word/token as a String (separated by spaces or newlines).
• sc.nextInt(), sc.nextDouble(), sc.nextLong(), sc.nextBoolean() read the next matching token and convert it.

3. Input in the 'Program input' field:
• Space / Tab: Separates individual tokens/values (e.g. '10 20' for two sc.nextInt() calls in the same line).
• Line break (Enter): Separates line-based inputs (e.g. for successive sc.nextLine() calls).
• Values are supplied before program execution starts. Interactive typing during execution is not supported in the browser.

cli.title: Terminal commands
cli.description: The editor expects Java source code, not commands. java, javac, jshell, jar, mvn, and gradle are not executed as terminal commands.

environment.title: OS access
environment.description: Local files, sockets, started processes, and native libraries are blocked by the browser runtime model.

runtimeFeatures.title: Dynamic runtime features
runtimeFeatures.description: Reflection-heavy code, dynamic class loading, and real Java threads are not reliable in this WebAssembly target.

stringsMath.title: Strings, Math, and big numbers
stringsMath.description: StringBuilder, String methods, Math functions, BigInteger, and BigDecimal work for typical console tasks.
